function.name: run_sql
function.description: Run a read-only ClickHouse SELECT and return its rows. Use it for every number you report. Query Gold marts (serving.mart_*) for totals and trends, Silver (silver.<table>) for detail rows. Compute totals, percentages, growth and rankings in the SQL itself. Tables and columns are in the DATA MAP.

function.name: list_datasets
function.description: List the datasets registered in the lakehouse catalog: slug, title, whether it comes from a primary or secondary source, and the Gold table it is served from. Optional keyword or source filter.

search.description: keyword to match in the title or slug

source.description: only datasets from primary or secondary sources

function.name: lakehouse_overview
function.description: Everything in the lakehouse by layer: the registered Bronze datasets, and every Silver and Gold table with its row count. Use it for "what data do we have?" and other overview questions.

function.name: describe_dataset
function.description: Describe one dataset by slug: title, description, source kind, which layers (Bronze/Silver/Gold) it is present in with row counts, and its documented columns.

function.name: get_lineage
function.description: Recorded lineage of a dataset or table: what feeds it and what it feeds (publisher, connector ingest, catalog registry, authored pipelines, views, Gold export). Every edge comes from a platform record; nothing is inferred from names.

slug.description: a dataset slug, or a table name such as serving.<table> or bronze.<table>

function.name: get_quality
function.description: Summary of the latest data quality check results (how many checks passed, warned or failed). Says so when no checks have run yet.

function.name: trigger_lakehouse_build
function.description: Rebuild the lakehouse layer by layer from what this deployment has: ingest every connector with an ingest spec into Bronze, run every authored pipeline, then export Gold to Iceberg (or the deployment's own build job when it has one). The result lists what was launched and what was skipped and why. Use only when the user asks to rebuild or refresh everything.

function.name: get_build_status
function.description: A log of the 10 most recent Dagster runs across all jobs, with status and start time. It does NOT give each pipeline's current state: to find failing pipelines use list_pipelines.

function.name: describe_mart
function.description: Gold marts (serving.*) that can be charted. With no argument: every mart with its row count. With `mart`: its columns split into dimensions (categories, time) and measures (numbers). Each column also has a kind (number, date, datetime, text); a date or datetime dimension can take a grain. Call this before create_chart.

function.name: create_chart
function.description: Create a chart card on a dashboard (/dashboards) from a Gold mart OR a saved SQL source (sqlSource, for data that combines several marts). The server writes the SQL from the columns you pick; you do not write SQL. Call describe_mart (or list_sql_sources) first to use columns that exist.

sqlSource.description: SQL source id (s_…) from list_sql_sources, instead of mart for a chart that combines several marts; set mart OR sqlSource, not both

param.description: the name of a parameter from list_parameters

dimension.description: the column to group by; or {param: <a list parameter whose values are columns of the data>} to let the viewer switch it

oneOf.description: a measure with its own aggregate, e.g. the average of stay beside the sum of visitors; its result column is named <aggregate>_<column> (avg_stay). Not for kpi, gauge, boxplot, maps, pivot or a table in rows mode

param.description: the name of a parameter from list_parameters

oneOf.description: a measure whose column the viewer switches: {column: {param: <list parameter>}, aggregate?}

metric.description: the name of a metric from list_metrics

oneOf.description: a saved metric by name (BI-2): the same number everywhere; it has its own aggregate, so no `aggregate` applies. The chart's table must be the metric's table. Prefer it to writing a measure yourself when list_metrics has one that matches

measures.description: the columns to aggregate (numbers); each is a column name (the chart's `aggregate` applies) or {column, aggregate}

param.description: the name of a parameter from list_parameters

breakdown.description: a second column to split by; or {param: <a list parameter>} to let the viewer switch it

map.description: map kinds only (geomap, pointmap, geoheat): id of a bundled map, one of dki-jakarta (Jakarta cities), id-provinces (Indonesian provinces), id-regencies (Indonesian kabupaten/kota)

lat.description: pointmap and geoheat only (required): the latitude column

lon.description: pointmap and geoheat only (required): the longitude column

param.description: the name of a parameter from list_parameters

limit.description: the number of groups; or {param: <a number parameter>} to let the viewer choose it (a whole number from 1 to 100 when the chart is read)

click.description: what a click on the chart does instead of the drill menu (not for text): {"kind":"dashboard","board":<dashboard id>,"column":<column of that dashboard the clicked value filters>}, {"kind":"query","id":<saved query id>}, or {"kind":"url","url":<https://… or a /path; {value} is replaced by the clicked value>}

grain.description: how to group a date or timestamp `dimension` (the column's kind is in describe_mart / list_sql_sources `columns`): minute, hour, day, week, month, quarter, year; or a part of the date: hour_of_day, day_of_week, day_of_month, week_of_year, month_of_year, quarter_of_year. Not for number or text columns; minute, hour and hour_of_day need a datetime column; a calendar chart takes day only; only bar, hbar, line, area, stacked, combo, waterfall, heatmap, pie, rose, funnel, treemap, radar and calendar charts take one. Omit for no grouping.

tableMode.description: table only: grouped (default) summarises by `dimension`; rows lists the rows themselves, 50 a page, in the `columns` you pick (no dimension or measures)

columns.description: table in rows mode: the columns to list, in order (1 to 30). pivot: the column fields (0 to 2)

rows.description: pivot only (required): the row fields, outermost first (1 to 3)

values.description: pivot only (required): what each cell shows (1 to 5). A pivot takes no dimension, measures or breakdown

totals.description: pivot only: none (default); grand adds the row, column and grand totals; all adds a subtotal for every outer group as well. Computed by the database, not by adding cells

sortColumn.description: table in rows mode: the column the rows are sorted by

columnSettings.description: table and pivot: per column name, {label, format (auto, number, percent, currency, date, link, image), decimals 0 to 6, width 60 to 800, wrap, hidden}. A link or image column must hold http(s) URLs

compare.description: kpi only: {"kind":"previous","dateColumn":<a date or timestamp column>,"period":day|week|month|quarter|year} compares the latest period that has data with the one before it and draws a trend line; or {"kind":"goal","value":<number>} compares with a goal

goodDirection.description: kpi only: which way is good, up (default) or down; colours the change

param.description: the name of a parameter from list_parameters

value.description: where on the value axis: a number, or {param: <a number parameter>}

referenceLines.description: up to 5 horizontal lines on the value axis (bar, hbar, line, area, stacked, combo), for example a target. Use a parameter for a line the viewer can move

segment.description: the name of a saved segment of the chart's table (BI-2): stands for its filters

min.description: between: a number or a date YYYY-MM-DD

filters.description: the chart's own filters (at most 20), always applied, whatever the dashboard's filters are; the same filters a dashboard takes, on columns of the chart's data. Use them for "only one category" or "only 2026"

mart.description: the Gold mart this question reads (give this or sqlSource)

sqlSource.description: the id of a saved SQL source (give this or mart)

dimension.description: a column of this question's data to line up with the chart's dimension: both dates, both text or both numbers; dates are lined up by the chart's time grain

oneOf.description: a measure with its own aggregate, e.g. the average of stay beside the sum of visitors; its result column is named <aggregate>_<column> (avg_stay). Not for kpi, gauge, boxplot, maps, pivot or a table in rows mode

param.description: the name of a parameter from list_parameters

oneOf.description: a measure whose column the viewer switches: {column: {param: <list parameter>}, aggregate?}

metric.description: the name of a metric from list_metrics

oneOf.description: a saved metric by name (BI-2): the same number everywhere; it has its own aggregate, so no `aggregate` applies. The chart's table must be the metric's table. Prefer it to writing a measure yourself when list_metrics has one that matches

measures.description: the columns to aggregate (numbers); each is a column name (the chart's `aggregate` applies) or {column, aggregate}

aggregate.description: for the measures that have none of their own; default sum

segment.description: the name of a saved segment of the chart's table (BI-2): stands for its filters

min.description: between: a number or a date YYYY-MM-DD

filters.description: this question's own filters (at most 20), on its own data

mart.description: a Gold mart to join to the chart's `mart` (call suggest_join first)

type.description: left keeps every row of what comes before; inner only the matches; right and full keep the joined table's unmatched rows too

left.description: a column of the chart's mart, or of an earlier join as <table>__<column>

right.description: a column of the table being joined

on.description: the pairs to match, all of them; at least one uses =

joins.description: up to four more Gold marts joined to this question's mart; not for a SQL source

label.description: the legend name, at most 60 characters

axis.description: which value axis; use right when its numbers are on another scale, like a rate beside visitors

layers.description: up to 4 more questions drawn on the same chart (bar, line, area or combo only), each from its own table or SQL source, lined up on the dimension's values: a value one lacks is a gap. For "visitors next to hotel rooms by month": the chart is visitors by month; one layer reads the rooms table by its month column. No breakdown, 'Other', steps or table calculation on a chart with layers. Unlike a join, layers never multiply rows

draw.description: with layers: how the chart's own series is drawn (default bar for a bar chart, line otherwise)

axis.description: with layers: which value axis the chart's own series uses (default left)

by.description: the dimension, a grouping of a table, or a measure's result name (the column name, or <aggregate>_<column> for a measure with its own aggregate)

sort.description: the order of the groups, in place of the default; with `limit` it keeps the first N in that order (top N: desc by a measure; bottom N: asc). Not for kpi, gauge, boxplot, maps, pivot or a table in rows mode

other.description: with `limit` and `sort`: gather every group past the limit into one group called Other, computed from the underlying rows (an average of Other is the average of those rows). bar, hbar, stacked, pie, rose, funnel, treemap and grouped table with one dimension only; not with a grain

column.description: a grouping or a measure of the result before this step

value.description: all but between: a number, a date YYYY-MM-DD, or text (eq and ne only)

filter.description: keep the rows that meet every condition

by.description: the groupings to keep, a subset of the result before (at least one)

column.description: a measure of the result before this step

measures.description: each is named <aggregate>_<column> in the result

summarise.description: group the result before this step again

items.description: give exactly one of filter and summarise

steps.description: up to two steps applied, in order, to the grouped result (for example: summarise by province, then keep totals over 1000). The chart's sort and limit then apply to the last step's result and may name only its columns (summarised measures are <aggregate>_<column>). Not for kpi, gauge, pivot, a raw table, maps, a time grain, a breakdown or 'Other'

mart.description: a Gold mart to join to the chart's `mart` (call suggest_join first)

type.description: left keeps every row of what comes before; inner only the matches; right and full keep the joined table's unmatched rows too

left.description: a column of the chart's mart, or of an earlier join as <table>__<column>

right.description: a column of the table being joined

on.description: the pairs to match, all of them; at least one uses =

joins.description: up to four more Gold marts joined to `mart`, read as one table: the chart's mart columns keep their names and a joined table's columns are <table>__<column> (a table joined twice: <table>2__<column>), usable as dimension, breakdown, measure, filter and in tables and pivots. Not for a SQL source. Joining on columns that are not unique in the joined table multiplies rows and so sums: prefer a max or avg for a joined table's measure. Calculated fields cannot use a joined column

grain.description: for a date or timestamp column

mode.description: auto: about ten bins with round edges; count: at most that many bins; width: bins of exactly that width

width.description: mode width: a positive number; the only mode for a SQL source

bin.description: for a number column, instead of a grain

groupings.description: table only: the columns a grouped table is grouped by (1 to 5), instead of dimension

mode.description: auto: about ten bins with round edges; count: at most that many bins; width: bins of exactly that width

width.description: mode width: a positive number; the only mode for a SQL source

bin.description: group the number `dimension` (or a pivot's first number row or column field) in ranges, for example visitors in bins of 500; the result value is each bin's lower edge. bar, hbar, line, area, stacked, combo, pie, rose, funnel, treemap, radar, waterfall, grouped table, pivot; not with a grain

mode.description: auto: about ten bins with round edges; count: at most that many bins; width: bins of exactly that width

width.description: mode width: a positive number; the only mode for a SQL source

size.description: auto, or the cell size in degrees: 0.01, 0.1, 1 or 10

grid.description: pointmap and geoheat only: group the points into square cells of latitude and longitude and draw one mark per cell at its centre, with the cell's value and point count

function.name: create_board
function.description: Create a new named dashboard (board). Returns its id for create_chart.

description.description: One-line purpose of the board, shown on the dashboard list page.

function.name: list_boards
function.description: List the dashboards (boards) that exist.

function.name: suggest_dashboard
function.description: Every Gold mart with its dimensions and measures at once, for proposing a set of dashboard charts.

function.name: list_charts
function.description: List the chart cards saved on dashboards.

function.name: list_sql_sources
function.description: List the dashboard SQL sources (saved SQL, usually combining several Gold marts) with their dimensions and measures. Use the id as sqlSource in create_chart. Users create SQL sources in Query Studio, not in chat.

function.name: suggest_join
function.description: Candidate column pairs for joining two Gold marts in a chart (`joins` of create_chart), best first: both columns in their tables' sorting keys with the same name and kind, then the same name and kind, then the same name. `suggested` marks the pairs to use; `coversRightKey` false means a row of the first mart may match several rows of the second, so sums of the second mart's columns multiply. Reads column metadata only.

right.description: the mart to join to it

function.name: delete_chart
function.description: Delete one saved chart card (by id). Built-in charts cannot be deleted. Needs human approval before it runs.

function.name: create_tab
function.description: Add a tab to a dashboard (board). On a dashboard with no tabs the first tab holds every chart already on it, so to separate some charts create a second tab as well and then move_charts_to_tab. The built-in dashboard has no tabs.

function.name: rename_tab
function.description: Rename a tab of a dashboard. The tab keeps its id, so charts and filters stay on it.

tab.description: the tab's id or its title, from list_boards

function.name: move_charts_to_tab
function.description: Put charts of a dashboard on one of its tabs, below what is already there. Charts are picked by id (list_charts); every one must be on this dashboard.

tab.description: the tab's id or its title

chartIds.description: ids of the charts to move

function.name: delete_tab
function.description: Delete a tab of a dashboard. Its charts move to the first remaining tab (none are deleted); a filter tied to it is tied to that tab instead. Needs human approval before it runs.

tab.description: the tab's id or its title

function.name: list_formula_functions
function.description: The formula language of calculated fields and every function it has (name, signature, one line of help, an example). Call it before writing a formula. You write formulas, never SQL.

function.name: list_calculated_fields
function.description: The calculated fields of one mart or SQL source (name, formula, whether it is one value per row or an aggregate, and its type). A chart uses one by naming it in dimension, breakdown or measures like a column.

mart.description: Gold mart name (from describe_mart); set mart OR sqlSource, not both

sqlSource.description: SQL source id (s_…) from list_sql_sources, instead of mart

function.name: validate_formula
function.description: Check a formula against a mart or SQL source without saving anything: returns ok with its level and type, or the message and the character position of the first mistake. Use it to fix a formula before create_calculated_field.

mart.description: Gold mart name (from describe_mart); set mart OR sqlSource, not both

sqlSource.description: SQL source id (s_…) from list_sql_sources, instead of mart

formula.description: the formula to check, in the formula language (see list_formula_functions)

name.description: the field's name, if it already has one (so a field that uses itself is caught)

function.name: create_calculated_field
function.description: Save a calculated field on a mart or SQL source from a formula in the formula language (see list_formula_functions); the server checks and compiles it. Then use its name in create_chart like a column: a per-row field can be a dimension, breakdown or measure; an aggregate field only a measure.

mart.description: Gold mart name (from describe_mart); set mart OR sqlSource, not both

sqlSource.description: SQL source id (s_…) from list_sql_sources, instead of mart

name.description: a name of letters, digits and _ (for example profit), not a column of the source; charts pick the field by it

formula.description: for example [revenue] - [cost], or Sum([revenue]) / CountDistinct([customer]); never SQL

function.name: update_calculated_field
function.description: Change the formula of a calculated field (by id from list_calculated_fields). The name stays; every chart using the field follows the new formula.

function.name: delete_calculated_field
function.description: Delete one calculated field (by id). Refused while a chart or another field uses it. Needs human approval before it runs.

function.name: list_metrics
function.description: The saved metrics (name, label, description, the table or SQL source they are computed from, their date column). A metric is one agreed definition of a number such as revenue. Call it BEFORE writing a query or a chart for a number the user names: if one matches, use it and name it in your answer; if none matches, say so before you write SQL.

mart.description: Gold mart name (from describe_mart); set mart OR sqlSource, not both

sqlSource.description: SQL source id (s_…) from list_sql_sources, instead of mart

function.name: describe_metric
function.description: One metric in full: its formula, filters, date column and default grain, and the charts and dashboards that use it.

function.name: query_metric
function.description: The value of a metric, read as the person you are helping (their access, masks and row filters apply). With no other argument it is one number. groupBy splits it by one column; grain (day, week, month, quarter, year) splits it by that period of the metric's date column; filters narrow it further. Say which metric you used.

groupBy.description: a column of the metric's table; with grain, a date column

segment.description: the name of a saved segment of the chart's table (BI-2): stands for its filters

min.description: between: a number or a date YYYY-MM-DD

filters.description: filters on columns of the metric's table, or a saved segment {segment}

function.name: create_metric
function.description: Save a reusable metric on a mart or SQL source. Only when the user asks for one; check list_metrics first so there is one definition per number. Needs the metric:write permission.

mart.description: Gold mart name (from describe_mart); set mart OR sqlSource, not both

sqlSource.description: SQL source id (s_…) from list_sql_sources, instead of mart

label.description: what people read, for example Total visitors

description.description: what it counts and how, at most 500 characters

formula.description: an AGGREGATE in the formula language, for example Sum([visitors]); never SQL (see list_formula_functions)

segment.description: the name of a saved segment of the chart's table (BI-2): stands for its filters

min.description: between: a number or a date YYYY-MM-DD

filters.description: the metric's own filters, applied to this metric's number only (or a saved segment {segment})

timeColumn.description: a date or timestamp column its period comparisons run on

name.description: letters, digits and _ (for example total_visitors), unique, not a column; charts pick the metric by it and it cannot change later

function.name: update_metric
function.description: Change a metric (by id). The name and the source stay; every chart that uses it follows the change at once, so say so. Send the whole definition.

mart.description: Gold mart name (from describe_mart); set mart OR sqlSource, not both

sqlSource.description: SQL source id (s_…) from list_sql_sources, instead of mart

label.description: what people read, for example Total visitors

description.description: what it counts and how, at most 500 characters

formula.description: an AGGREGATE in the formula language, for example Sum([visitors]); never SQL (see list_formula_functions)

segment.description: the name of a saved segment of the chart's table (BI-2): stands for its filters

min.description: between: a number or a date YYYY-MM-DD

filters.description: the metric's own filters, applied to this metric's number only (or a saved segment {segment})

timeColumn.description: a date or timestamp column its period comparisons run on

function.name: delete_metric
function.description: Delete one metric (by id). Refused while a chart uses it. Needs human approval before it runs.

function.name: create_value_group
function.description: Gather chosen values of a text column under names of your own (for example six provinces as Java) and save it as a field of the source. Then use its name in create_chart as dimension or breakdown, like a column. It is a text column, so not a measure. Take the values from run_sql or describe_mart, never invent them.

mart.description: Gold mart name (from describe_mart); set mart OR sqlSource, not both

sqlSource.description: SQL source id (s_…) from list_sql_sources, instead of mart

name.description: a name of letters, digits and _ (for example region_group), not a column of the source; charts pick the group by it like a column

column.description: a text column of the source

name.description: what the values are shown as, for example Java

values.description: values of the column exactly as spelled; a value belongs to one group only; at most 2000 in all

rest.description: keep: values in no group keep their own name; other: they are shown as Other

function.name: list_hierarchies
function.description: The hierarchies of one mart or SQL source: named, ordered lists of columns (for example province, city, place) that a chart can be drilled down through by clicking a value.

mart.description: Gold mart name (from describe_mart); set mart OR sqlSource, not both

sqlSource.description: SQL source id (s_…) from list_sql_sources, instead of mart

function.name: create_hierarchy
function.description: Save a hierarchy on a mart or SQL source. A viewer can then drill down a chart whose dimension is one of its levels. Charts do not store it, so it never breaks a chart.

mart.description: Gold mart name (from describe_mart); set mart OR sqlSource, not both

sqlSource.description: SQL source id (s_…) from list_sql_sources, instead of mart

levels.description: 2 to 6 columns of the source, outermost first (province, city, place)

function.name: delete_hierarchy
function.description: Delete one hierarchy (by id from list_hierarchies). No chart depends on it. Needs human approval before it runs.

function.name: list_parameters
function.description: The parameters of the deployment: named values (a number, text, a date, or a choice from a list) that a viewer changes on a dashboard and that a formula ({name}), a chart's limit, a reference line or a column switch can read. Use before create_chart to reuse one.

function.name: create_parameter
function.description: Define a parameter. Then use it in a formula as {name}, as a chart's limit, as a reference line (referenceLines) or, for a list, as the dimension, breakdown or a measure's column.

name.description: letters, digits and _, at most 64; a formula writes it as {name}. Cannot be changed later

default.description: the value when nobody chose one; a date is YYYY-MM-DD; a list default is one of the values

values.description: list: the choices, all text or all numbers. For a parameter that switches a chart's column, the values are column names of the chart's data (take them from describe_mart)

function.name: update_parameter
function.description: Change a parameter (by id): its label, default, bounds or values. Send every field. Its name and type stay.

name.description: letters, digits and _, at most 64; a formula writes it as {name}. Cannot be changed later

default.description: the value when nobody chose one; a date is YYYY-MM-DD; a list default is one of the values

values.description: list: the choices, all text or all numbers. For a parameter that switches a chart's column, the values are column names of the chart's data (take them from describe_mart)

function.name: delete_parameter
function.description: Delete one parameter (by id from list_parameters). Refused while a formula, a chart or a dashboard uses it. Needs human approval before it runs.

function.name: list_alert_rules
function.description: List every alert rule (threshold alerts) and digest (scheduled summaries), with whether each is enabled.

function.name: create_alert_rule
function.description: Create an alert or digest rule. Alert (type=alert): mart, measure, agg, op and threshold; it watches that aggregate. Or give metric (a name from list_metrics) with op and threshold, and the alert watches that metric instead (it is read with the fixed viewer role every alert uses, not with the user's access). Digest (type=digest): board, the dashboard to summarise. Delivered by webhook (target=URL) or email (target=address).

measure.description: measure column to watch, for type=alert

metric.description: the name of a metric to watch, for type=alert, instead of mart/measure/agg

target.description: webhook URL or email address to deliver to

function.name: update_alert_rule
function.description: Change a saved alert or digest rule (by id). Send every field, as for create_alert_rule, with the new values. list_alert_rules gives the ids.

metric.description: the name of a metric to watch instead of mart/measure/agg

function.name: delete_alert_rule
function.description: Delete an alert or digest rule permanently (by id). Needs human approval before it runs.

function.name: run_alert_rule
function.description: Evaluate one alert or digest rule now (by id). If its condition holds, the webhook or email is really sent.

function.name: list_connectors
function.description: List the registered data connectors (sources and targets) and their health.

function.name: create_connector
function.description: Register a new connector. The server creates the connector id and derives the credential reference names from it: choose a source (env/file) and kind per slot, never send a secret or secretRef. The names the operator must provide are returned once.

credential.description: credential spec; the server derives the reference names from the connector id

secondary.description: second slot, e.g. an S3 secret key; optional

function.name: test_connector
function.description: Run a real connection test on a connector (by id). PostgreSQL, S3-compatible object storage, MySQL/MariaDB, SQL Server and REST sources can be dialled; any other type returns supported:false instead of a made-up result.

function.name: delete_connector
function.description: Delete a connector registration permanently (by id). Needs human approval before it runs.

function.name: list_pipelines
function.description: List every pipeline (Dagster jobs and pipelines authored in the console) with its latest status (e.g. failed, completed), schedule, and last and next run. Use it to answer which pipelines are failing or healthy.

function.name: list_pipeline_runs
function.description: The latest runs (up to 30) of one pipeline (by id), with status and times.

function.name: trigger_pipeline
function.description: Run one pipeline now (by id). Different from trigger_lakehouse_build, which always runs the main Bronze -> Silver -> Gold rebuild. Optional runConfig (object) overrides the job's defaults — validated against the job's config schema before launch; an invalid config fails with a structured 400.

function.name: retry_pipeline_run
function.description: Re-run a finished pipeline run (by runId): every step, only the failed steps (with fromFailure, failed runs only), or a named subset of steps (with stepKeys).

function.name: pause_pipeline
function.description: Pause a pipeline's schedule (by id). Needs human approval before it runs.

function.name: resume_pipeline
function.description: Resume a paused pipeline's schedule (by id).

function.name: cancel_pipeline_run
function.description: Stop a running pipeline run (by runId). Needs human approval before it runs.

function.name: save_query
function.description: Save a SQL query under a name, to run again later with run_saved_query.

function.name: list_saved_queries
function.description: List the saved queries.

function.name: run_saved_query
function.description: Run a saved query (by id) and return its rows. Only read-only statements run, as in Query Studio.

function.name: get_audit_history
function.description: Audit history: Dagster pipeline runs plus copilot and console actions (who did what, when, and the outcome).

function.name: list_classification_rules
function.description: Data classification per asset and column (public/internal/confidential/restricted): what was observed plus the rules that were written.

function.name: list_quality_rules
function.description: Data quality rules (completeness, uniqueness, ...) and their last results: what was observed plus the rules that were written.

function.name: get_cdc_health
function.description: Health of CDC replication slots per connector: status, lag and WAL retained, to catch a stuck slot before it fills the source database's disk.

function.name: get_maintenance_metrics
function.description: History of Bronze Iceberg maintenance runs (remove_orphan_files): orphan data and manifest files removed per table. expire_snapshots is refused by ClickHouse for catalog-managed Iceberg tables and is recorded as skipped. Read-only.

function.name: run_bronze_maintenance
function.description: Run Bronze maintenance now (Dagster bronze_maintenance_job). This APPLIES changes: orphan Iceberg data and manifest files are deleted. It is not a dry run. Needs human approval before it runs.

function.name: list_workloads
function.description: ClickHouse queries running right now, with the ids ("w-<n>") kill_query uses.

function.name: kill_query
function.description: Stop one running ClickHouse query (a real KILL QUERY, by id from list_workloads, e.g. "w-0"). Needs human approval before it runs.

function.name: export_gold_mart
function.description: Export one Gold mart (serving.<mart>) to its Iceberg Gold table through Lakekeeper. Append-only: running it again adds the rows again with a new _exported_at; it does not replace them.

function.name: get_gold_export
function.description: Read a Gold Iceberg table back (by mart) through Lakekeeper: its row count and format version, independent of ClickHouse.

function.name: draft_policy
function.description: Draft a new governance policy. It is always saved as a draft, never active; activating it stays a human action in the console (Governance -> Policies).

subjects.description: who or what the policy applies to

function.name: draft_classification_rule
function.description: Write a new classification or masking rule for an asset (optionally one column). It is saved as needs-review; review stays a human action in the console.

function.name: draft_quality_rule
function.description: Write a new data quality rule for an asset. A new rule is saved as a warning (not yet evaluated).

function.name: get_ingest_spec
function.description: Read a connector's ingest spec: its adapter (sql, cdc, files, rest, sheets, mongodb, kafka, sftp), ingest mode, dial (how to reach the source), the source objects it ingests and the Bronze table each lands in, and its schedule. Null fields mean ingest was never set up.

function.name: set_ingest_spec
function.description: Set what a connector ingests into Bronze. Call get_ingest_spec and discover_source first. adapter and dial must match the connector's type; each source object names a source table (or endpoint, file) and the Bronze table it lands in. When you send a connector's source objects again (for example to add a table), keep each object's loadMode and primaryKey exactly as get_ingest_spec returned them: an object sent without a loadMode goes back to replace. Example for a Postgres table: adapter "sql", ingestMode "batch", dial {"driver":"postgres","host":"db","port":5432,"database":"shop","user":"reader"}, sourceObjects [{"name":"public.orders","target":"orders"}], scheduleCron "0 * * * *". The server validates the dial and refuses internal addresses. This tool never carries a credential, so it cannot change where a connector points (adapter, host, port, database, endpoint, bucket, base URL or brokers): such a change is refused with a conflict and is made in the console, where the credentials are entered again.

dial.description: how to reach the source; fields depend on the adapter

loadMode.description: how each run writes the table; omitted means replace

primaryKey.description: columns that identify one row; needed by replace_dedup, incremental_dedup and history

target.description: Bronze table name it lands in

scheduleCron.description: cron schedule for batch ingest, optional

function.name: discover_source
function.description: Connect to a connector's source and list the tables (and their columns) that could be ingested. Read-only on the source. Returns supported:false for source types this build cannot list.

schema.description: optional schema to list, e.g. public

function.name: run_ingest
function.description: Run one connector's ingest now: reads its source objects into Bronze (the same as Run now in the console). The connector needs an ingest spec first. A CDC connector returns supported:false: Debezium streams it continuously.

function.name: list_ingest_runs
function.description: Recent ingest runs of one connector: when each ran, which object, rows written, and success or the reason it failed.

function.name: rotate_connector_credential
function.description: Point a connector's credential slot at a new credential. The server derives the credential name from the connector id; you choose only the slot, where it is read from (env or file) and its kind. The new credential is tested before it is saved. Needs human approval before it runs.

function.name: create_pipeline
function.description: Author a new pipeline that reads a source table, applies transforms and writes a target table. It is saved as a draft; mark_pipeline_ready makes it runnable. Zones: bronze, silver, gold. Transforms use a fixed vocabulary, one per entry: dedupe(col), filter(col = 'value') with = != < > <= >=, rename(old,new), cast(col,Int64) with String Int32 Int64 Float64 Boolean Date DateTime UUID, select(col1,col2).

function.name: get_pipeline
function.description: One pipeline's detail: its definition (source, transforms, target), op graph, schedule and recent runs.

id.description: pipeline id from list_pipelines (pl-… for an authored pipeline, or a Dagster job name)

function.name: mark_pipeline_ready
function.description: Move an authored pipeline (pl-…) from draft to ready, so the orchestrator builds a job for it and trigger_pipeline can run it.

function.name: list_iceberg_tables
function.description: The Iceberg tables in the lakehouse warehouse (Lakekeeper): with namespace, that namespace's tables; without, every namespace with its tables, including Bronze and exported Gold. Each table has its format version, current snapshot, last update, files, records and size.

function.name: describe_iceberg_table
function.description: One Iceberg table: schema (columns and types), partition spec, and recent snapshots with their operation, time and record counts.

function.name: get_table_maintenance
function.description: One Iceberg table's maintenance policy (snapshots to keep, orphan-file age, small-file compaction, schedule) and its last maintenance status.

function.name: set_table_maintenance
function.description: Set one Iceberg table's maintenance policy, read by the nightly maintenance job. Send the whole policy.

orphanAgeHours.description: remove orphan files older than this, optional

function.name: get_capacity
function.description: Storage capacity: each object-storage bucket's size and growth from the daily capacity snapshot, and ClickHouse's bytes on disk.

function.name: ask_user
function.description: Ask the user which reading of an unclear word they mean, with two to four options taken from the DATA MAP. Use it only when a word fits two or more tables, columns or values and nothing in the DATA MAP or THIS USER'S WORDS settles it. Ask once, run no query in that turn, and write nothing else after the call.

term.description: the unclear word, as the user wrote it (1 to 60 characters)

question.description: one sentence asking which they mean (at most 200 characters)

options.description: the readings to choose from: names from the DATA MAP, each 1 to 80 characters

function.name: propose_sql
function.description: Propose the whole corrected statement once, with one sentence saying what was wrong. The server checks that it would run for this user, and the person sees it as a diff and accepts or rejects it. It is never run by you or by the server. Use it only for a query the person asked you to fix.

sql.description: the whole corrected statement, not a fragment (1 to 20000 characters)

reason.description: one sentence saying what was wrong (1 to 300 characters)

engine.description: the engine the statement is for
